questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Hima was so affected by the movie __that she has not speak a word__ to anyone for a week.

options.text: that she has not been spoken a word
that she did not speak a word

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**that she did not speak a word**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence has an incorrect phrase: "**she has not speak a word**".
 
• The setting of the sentence is in the past. The movie affected Hima in the past and the outcome (her not speaking) is also in the past.
 
• The present perfect tense "**has not spoken**" suggests an action started in the past and continues to the present, which is not the case here. The sentence refers to a specific past week.
 
• '**Option 4**' corrects this by using the simple past tense "**did not speak**", which indicates that Hima didn’t speak in that specific past time period (for a week), after she watched the movie.
 
• The simple past tense is also correct because it refers to a fully completed action.

Therefore, the correct answer is - '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 'Option 1' ("**that she has not been spoken a word**") is incorrect because it implies that no one has spoken to her, rather than her not speaking, and it misplaces the blame for her silence.
 
• 'Option 2' ("**that she is speaking**") is incorrect because it contradicts the meaning of the sentence. It suggests that she is currently speaking, which is wrong as per the statement.
 
• 'Option 3' ("**that she has been speaking**") also contradicts the meaning of the sentence. Similar to Option 2, it suggests that she has been talking continuously, which is the opposite of the intended meaning.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Evelyn became very angry; it seemed to her that she ______ never fulfil her dream of being a great musician.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'would.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the past tense.
 
• It conveys the meaning that something happened in the past, and then, standing in that past time, it was mentioned as a future possibility.
 
• We often use **would (or the contracted form 'd)** in the main clause of a conditional sentence when we talk about imagined situations.
 
 
• **Example**: *I **would**__ love to see both.*
 
 
 
• Hence, ‘**would**’ is the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.
 
• The correct answer is option (1).

**Correct sentence**: *“Evelyn became very angry; it seemed to her that she __**would**__ never fulfill her dream of being a great musician.”*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__** *

__
 
• ‘Can’ and ‘will’ are in present and future form.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Can__ you ride a bicycle?*
 
• *She __will__ come tomorrow.*
 
 
 
• "Ought to" is a modal verb phrase that is used to indicate a moral obligation, duty, or strong recommendation. It does not make sense for the given sentence.
 __
 
• Example:* You ought to__ visit your parents more often.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A Penelope’s web
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e.** 'An endless job'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"A Penelope's web"** is an idiom that comes from the ancient Greek myth involving Penelope, the wife of Odysseus. 
 
• In English, the phrase means "an endless, seemingly futile task" (अनंत, निरर्थक कार्य जो कभी समयाप्त नहीं होता).
 
 
• **Example: **Cleaning John's vast, antiquated mansion felt like a Penelope's web; it seemed like the task would never come to an end.
 
• The term **"endless job"** means a task or an assignment that appears to have no definitive ending or conclusion (अनंत कार्य).
 
 
 
• **Example:** Jack described his current project as an endless job, as new issues continued to resurface preventing him from making significant progress.

Therefore, the **correct answer **is - **'An endless job'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'A daily job' **(Option 1) refers to work that is performed on a daily basis, typically involving routine tasks (दैनिक काम).
 
• **'An important job' **(Option 2) implies work that is highly valuable or holds a significant level of responsibility (महत्वपूर्ण कार्य).
 
• **'A meaningless job'** (Option 4) defines work that lacks purpose or value, often appearing futile or insignificant (बेअर्थ काम).

Don’t go to the neighbour’s garden, ______ not allowed to go there.
questions.solution:

• **​**The sentence is basically saying **"You are not allowed to go there."**
 
• **"You’re" **is a contraction of **'you are', **which communicates the intended meaning perfectly in this context.
 
 
• **Example**: *You need to wear seat belts when **you're**__ in the car.*
 
 
 
• Hence, filling the blank with **"you're" **will complete the sentence correctly as: **"Don’t go to the neighbour’s garden, you’re not allowed to go there."**
 
• So, the correct answer is **"Option 4."**

 

**Correct sentence: ***Don’t go to the neighbour’s garden, __**you're**__ not allowed to go there.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "revealed."**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "Revealed" means to make something known that was secret or unknown before. ((गुप्‍त या पूर्वतः अज्ञात वस्‍तु को) प्रकट करना, रहस्‍य खोल लेना)
 
 
• Example: *She **revealed**__ her history to him because she thought it was important.*
 
 
 
• The sentence conveys that after everything was finished, the mould was taken out and a flawlessly shaped object was shown.
 
• The correct answer is option 3.
 
• Correct passage:

The Chinese rulers were called the Shang. Chinese civilisation is one of the oldest civilisations of the world which __flourished__ in north-east China. The Chinese had thought __up__ a very clever way of casting weapons and pots which were made of bronze. These people first made a rough model of the object they wanted to cast or make. Then, they shaped the clay mould closely __around__ the prepared model. When the clay was dry, the mould was __removed__ and cut into pieces. These carved pieces were filled with molten bronze and left to cool down. In the final process, the mould was removed and a perfectly formed object was __**revealed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Dropped: **to let something fall. (गिराना, गिरने देना)
 
• **Disclosed: **to tell something to somebody or to make something known publicly. (किसी को कोई बात बताना या सार्वजनिक रूप से प्रकट करना)
 
• **Divulged: **to tell something that is secret. (गुप्‍त बात बताना, (रहस्‍य) प्रकट करना)
